main_text.head: SECT. VI.
main_text.p: Cafius 59Sed posse videtur reliquis qui superfunt tribus modis : Irritatione sc. Superioris, Cessatione Materiæ, & Relaxatione Partis. Cafius ergo Tertius est de solutione vinculi per Irritationem à Superiore factam. Significat autem Irri-tatio (sic enim, Barbare licet, cum Ca-fuistis loquendum est,) actum legitimi superioris, quo authoritate sua irritum facit sive annullat juramentum à subdito sine ipsius consensu præstitum. Refcinde-re enim posse legitimum superiorem vota & juramenta eorum qui sub ipsorum sunt potestate, & non sui juris, fuse docet{c}Num.30. hoc ipso capite Moses : uti nos ubi de Causa efficiente egimus{d}Præleét.[?] 4.num.f. ante ostendimus. Ratio est, quia is qui alienæ potestati subest, non est sui juris, non habet potestatem se obligandi in iis rebus in quibus subest, nisi ex voluntate superioris cui subest : & proinde non debet aliquo actu suo inducere sibi obligationem sine illius consensu, vel expresso, vel rationa-

page.notes: Marginal reference marks: the mark in the text after "docet" is read as "c", but the margin mark beside it reads like "e" (so the note may belong to "e"); the printed letter in the text is therefore doubtful. The "Præleét." abbreviation is uncertain (the ligature is hard to read). Page number and running head are as printed. The text ends with the broken word "rationa-" on the last line; there is no catchword or signature visible.
